backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with XGBRegressor. Use base_score=0.5, learning_rate=0.05, and max_depth=6.
backlog.title: XGBoost implementation

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with LightGBM's LGBMRegressor. Use num_leaves=31, learning_rate=0.05, and feature_fraction=0.8.
backlog.title: LightGBM implementation

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with CatBoostRegressor. Use learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, and iterations=1000.
backlog.title: CatBoost implementation

backlog.spec: Apply StandardScaler to the train_y values before fitting. Store the mean and scale to transform the test_smiles predictions.
backlog.title: Standardization of Target

backlog.spec: Apply np.log1p to the target values to handle potential skewness, then use np.expm1 to reverse the transformation on predictions.
backlog.title: Log Transformation

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000 to reduce variance in the random forest.
backlog.title: Increase Trees

backlog.spec: Decrease MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 0.2 to increase the diversity of trees in the Random Forest.
backlog.title: Reduce Max Features

backlog.spec: Increase MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF from 1 to 5 to prevent over-fitting to specific molecules.
backlog.title: Increase Min Samples Leaf

backlog.spec: Change RADIUS from 2 to 3 to capture larger structural environments.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3

backlog.spec: Change N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 to reduce dimensionality and potential noise.
backlog.title: Morgan Bits 1024

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with max_depth=8 and learning_rate=0.01.
backlog.title: XGBoost Depth 8

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.8.
backlog.title: LightGBM subsample

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor with depth=10 and l2_leaf_reg=3.
backlog.title: CatBoost depth 10

backlog.spec: Add max_depth=15 to RandomForestRegressor to limit tree growth.
backlog.title: Random Forest Max Depth

backlog.spec: Concatenate Morgan fingerprints with RDKit's Descriptors (MolDescriptors.CalcProperties).
backlog.title: Fingerprint Concatenation

backlog.spec: Use a fixed set of 200 RDKit descriptors as the input feature vector instead of fingerprints.
backlog.title: Descriptor Count

backlog.spec: Clip train_y values to the 1st and 99th percentiles to remove outliers before training.
backlog.title: Target Clipping

backlog.spec: Implement a simple internal validation split in fit_predict to use early stopping with XGBRegressor.
backlog.title: XGBoost Early Stopping

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with importance_type='gain'.
backlog.title: LightGBM Feature Importance

backlog.spec: Use sample_weight in RandomForestRegressor.fit based on the variance of the targets.
backlog.title: Weighted Random Forest

backlog.spec: Ensure all RDKit descriptors are imputed with the median value if any are NaN.
backlog.title: Median Imputation

backlog.spec: If the target is bounded (e.g., 0 to 1), apply a logit transform before training.
backlog.title: Logit Transform

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with gamma=0.1 for minimum loss reduction requirement.
backlog.title: XGBoost Gamma

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with min_data_in_leaf=50.
backlog.title: LightGBM Min Data in Leaf

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor with baggings_count=5 and bag_leaf_sample=0.8.
backlog.title: CatBoost Bagging

backlog.spec: Use the 'ccf' (cumulative class frequency) or similar approach to bias toward smaller values if the distribution is skewed.
backlog.title: Random Forest CCF

backlog.spec: Use StandardScaler on the descriptors if using RDKit descriptors.
backlog.title: Feature Scaling

backlog.spec: Experiment with learning_rate=0.02 and num_boost_round=1000 for XGBoost.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter Tuning (Manual)

backlog.spec: Append the heavy atom count and num_hydrogen count as two extra features to the fingerprint vector.
backlog.title: Morgan Fingerprint + Count

backlog.spec: Set max_features='sqrt' for RandomForestRegressor.
backlog.title: Random Forest sqrt Features

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor. ExtraTrees is similar to Random Forest but chooses splits randomly for each feature, which can often provide better generalization for small datasets like this one. Keep all other parameters (N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES, log1p transform) the same.
backlog.title: ExtraTreesRegressor replacement

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000. Since the training time is 20 seconds and we have a 10-minute limit for 15 fits, 1000 trees per fit should still fit within the time budget. More trees can reduce the variance of the prediction.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES to 1000

backlog.spec: Increase the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3. This captures larger local molecular environments. Keep the bit size at 2048.
backlog.title: Morgan Radius 3 Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Decrease N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. Reducing the bit space can sometimes act as a form of dimensionality reduction or collision-based regularization, which might be beneficial given the small number of molecules.
backlog.title: Morgan Bits 1024

backlog.spec: Apply a StandardScalar transformation to the log1p-transformed targets (subtract mean, divide by std) before training, and apply the same transformation parameters to the predictions before using expm1. This ensures the target distribution is centered and scaled.
backlog.title: Standardize log1p targets

backlog.spec: Explicitly set max_depth=15 in the RandomForestRegressor. Restricting the depth can prevent the trees from over-fitting to noise in the small training set of 970 molecules.
backlog.title: Max Depth Constraint

backlog.spec: Increase min_samples_leaf from 1 to 5. This forces each leaf to represent a larger number of molecules, smoothing the regression surface and potentially improving generalization on unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Min Samples Leaf Constraint

backlog.spec: Instead of log1p, transform the targets using a rank-based transformation (e.g., mapping targets to their percentile ranks or a sigmoid of the ranks) before training. This focuses the model on learning the correct ordering of clearance values.
backlog.title: Rank-based Target Transformation

backlog.spec: Clip the log1p-transformed target values to the 1st and 99th percentiles before training. This removes outliers that might be disproportionately influencing the Random Forest's split points.
backlog.title: Target Clipping

backlog.spec: Combine the 2048 Morgan bits with a set of standard RDKit descriptors (e.g., MolWt, LogP, HBD, HBA, TPSA). The featurize function should return the concatenated numpy array of Morgan bits and the descriptor values.
backlog.title: Hybrid Feature: Morgan + RDKit Descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor. ExtraTrees often performs better in regression tasks because it selects features randomly at each split, providing an additional layer of ensemble diversity over Random Forest's standard feature sampling.
backlog.title: ExtraTreesRegressor

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000. While more trees increase computational time, the noise in the evaluation is low enough that the reduction in variance from a larger forest might lead to a more stable and slightly lower mean loss.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES to 1000

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. Reducing the dimensionality of the Morgan fingerprint can sometimes act as a form of implicit regularization and can be useful if the 2048-bit space is too sparse for the 970 molecules provided.
backlog.title: Morgan Bits to 1024

backlog.spec: After applying np.log1p to the training targets, use StandardScaler from sklearn to normalize the features to zero mean and unit variance. This may help the forest split points more consistently across different scales of chemical properties.
backlog.title: Standardize log1p targets

backlog.spec: Set max_depth to a specific value, e.g., 15 or 20. By default, RF grows trees until leaves are pure; limiting depth can prevent the model from over-fitting to specific noise in the small training set.
backlog.title: Random Forest Max Depth Constraint

backlog.spec: Generate MACCS keys (2048 bits) using RDKit and concatenate them with the existing Morgan fingerprints and RDKit properties. This provides a structural 'checklist' of chemical motifs that complements the circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: MACCS Keys + Morgan

backlog.spec: Generate RDKit's Atom Pair fingerprints and concatenate them with the Morgan fingerprints. Atom pairs capture linear distances and connectivity that circular fingerprints might miss in certain linear molecules.
backlog.title: Atom Pair Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the log1p transform with a QuantileTransformer (output_distribution='normal'). This maps the training targets to a normal distribution, which can be very effective for regression problems with non-normal distributions and outliers.
backlog.title: Quantile Transformer

backlog.spec: Instead of using all RDKit Properties equally, identify the top 10 most correlated properties with the target and only concatenate those with the Morgan fingerprints to reduce noise from irrelevant descriptors.
backlog.title: Feature Weighting (Rank-based)

backlog.spec: Train both a RandomForestRegressor and an ExtraTreesRegressor. In fit_predict, return the average of their predictions. This diversity in the ensembling method can often produce a more robust result than either model alone.
backlog.title: Weighted Ensemble (RF + ExtraTrees)

backlog.spec: Increase the N_TREES constant from 300 to 1000. This increases the capacity of the ensemble to capture complex patterns in the Morgan fingerprints and RDKit descriptors without significantly increasing the risk of overfitting in a 5-fold cross-validation scheme.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES to 1000

backlog.spec: Change the prediction formula from a simple average (0.5 * RF + 0.5 * ET) to a weighted average. Since ExtraTrees often provides higher variance but potentially better coverage, try a 0.3 * RF + 0.7 * ET weight to see if it improves the Spearman correlation.
backlog.title: Weighted Ensemble of RF and ET

backlog.spec: Apply a StandardScaler (mean=0, std=1) to the y values after the log1p transformation. Standardizing the target distribution can sometimes help regression models converge more stably and improve the ranking of predicted values.
backlog.title: Standardize log1p targets

backlog.spec: Introduce a max_depth parameter (e.g., max_depth=20) to the RandomForestRegressor and ExtraTreesRegressor. Setting a hard limit on depth can prevent individual trees from becoming too complex and over-fitting the noise in the small training set.
backlog.title: Random Forest Max Depth Constraint

backlog.spec: Implement a 'Corrected Correlation Forest' approach by using the Spearman correlation as a custom metric or by focusing on the ordering of the targets. A simpler version is to use the median of the trees' predictions instead of the mean to increase robustness to outliers.
backlog.title: Random Forest CCF

backlog.spec: Prioritize the RDKit descriptors by concatenating them at the beginning of the feature vector and applying a small multiplier to the Morgan fingerprint bits. Alternatively, try to select only the top 100 features using a simple correlation with the target.
backlog.title: Custom Feature Weighting

backlog.spec: Even though the search for GBMs has been poor, try a LightGBMRegressor with a very small learning_rate (e.g., 0.005) and a high number of estimators (e.g., 2000) with a 'step' learning rate schedule to see if it can outperform the RF/ET ensemble.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Schedule for GBM (Hybrid)

backlog.spec: Concatenate the 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint with a 1024-bit version of the same fingerprint but with different radii (e.g., radius 1 and radius 2) to capture different scales of molecular environments simultaneously.
backlog.title: Mixed Precision Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Set max_features to a smaller float like 0.1 instead of 'sqrt' for the ExtraTreesRegressor. This forces the trees to be more decorrelated from each other, potentially improving the ensemble's ability to generalize to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees Diversity Boost

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000 for both RandomForestRegressor and ExtraTreesRegressor. This is a direct way to reduce variance in the ensemble, which may improve the Spearman correlation on the unseen test skeletons.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES to 1000

backlog.spec: After applying the np.log1p transform to the training targets, subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation of the transformed values. This standardizes the target distribution to unit variance and zero mean before fitting the models.
backlog.title: Standardize log1p targets

backlog.spec: Keep RandomForestRegressor with max_features='sqrt' but change ExtraTreesRegressor to use max_features=0.7. ExtraTrees is designed to be more diverse when it samples more features per split, while Random Forest benefits from the high-variance reduction of 'sqrt'.
backlog.title: Separate max_features for RF and ET

backlog.spec: Modify the featurize function to also compute RDKit MACCS keys. Concatenate the Morgan fingerprint (2048 bits), the MACCS keys (167 bits), and the RDKit descriptors into a single feature vector for each molecule.
backlog.title: MACCS + Morgan + Descriptors

backlog.spec: Instead of a 0.5/0.5 average, use a weighted sum of the predictions from RandomForestRegressor and ExtraTreesRegressor. Experiment with weights like 0.7/0.3 or 0.6/0.4, as one model might be significantly more robust than the other for this specific regression task.
backlog.title: Weighted ensemble of RF and ET

backlog.spec: Change N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. Reducing the bit space can sometimes lead to higher density information and faster training, potentially avoiding noise in the very high dimensions of the 2048-bit space.
backlog.title: Standardize Morgan bits to 1024

backlog.spec: Replace the np.log1p(y) transformation with a logit transform (or a sigmoid-scaled transform if the data is strictly positive). Since the output is clearance, ensure the input to the logit transform is scaled to the (0, 1) range, then exp the output back.
backlog.title: Logit transform target

backlog.spec: Implement a simple Cost- benefit analysis (CCF) approach for the ensemble: instead of simple averaging, slightly weight the predictions based on the mean squared error of each model's performance on the validation set (within the fit_predict loop).
backlog.title: Random Forest CCF (Cost- beneficio)

backlog.spec: Add a third model to the ensemble: a LightGBMRegressor with a very small number of trees (e.g., 100) and a high learning rate. Average its predictions with the existing RF and ExtraTrees predictions (e.g., weights 0.33, 0.33, 0.34).
backlog.title: Small-weight GBM in rank blend

backlog.spec: Since GBMs were rejected before, try a LightGBMRegressor with a much smaller learning rate (e.g., 0.01) and a 'step' or 'exponential' learning rate schedule if the package supports it, or simply a very high number of trees (e.g., 1500) with a low learning rate to see if it overcomes the previous rejection.
backlog.title: Learning Rate Schedule for GBM

backlog.spec: Modify the featurize function to include RDKit MACCS keys. Since the standard 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint is already used, the MACCS keys (166 bits) should be concatenated as a separate block of bits. This provides structural keys that may capture different chemical motifs than the Morgan circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: MACCS + Morgan + Descriptors

backlog.spec: Concatenate two Morgan fingerprints: one with radius 1 (1024 bits) and one with radius 2 (2048 bits). This allows the model to see local atom environments and larger circular environments as distinct features simultaneously.
backlog.title: Radius-1 Morgan + Radius-2 Morgan

backlog.spec: After applying np.log1p to the target values, use StandardScaler from scikit-learn to normalize the training targets to zero mean and unit variance. Then, apply the same transformation to the test set during prediction (preserving the log1p transformation as part of the pipeline).
backlog.title: Standardize Log1p Targets

backlog.spec: Instead of a 0.5/0.5 average of RF and ExtraTrees, use a weighted sum where the weights are optimized to favor the ExtraTreesRegressor (e.g., 0.6*ET + 0.4*RF), as ExtraTrees often provides better variance reduction in regression tasks.
backlog.title: Balanced Ensemble Weights

backlog.spec: Implement a Co-occurrence Count Feature (CCF) logic or a simple heuristic: for each molecule, calculate the count of specific functional groups (e.g., aromatic rings, hydroxyl groups) using RDKit and append these counts as additional features to the Morgan fingerprint.
backlog.title: Multi-Tree Feature Correlation (CCF)

backlog.spec: Before applying the log1p transform, clip the training targets to the 1st and 99th percentiles. This removes potential outliers that might disproportionately influence the tree splits during training, making the model more robust to extreme values.
backlog.title: Target Percentile Clipping

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed N_TREES, use a multi-stage training approach or a very high tree count (e.g., 1500) with a very high min_samples_leaf (e.g., 10) to prevent overfitting on the small dataset (970 molecules).
backlog.title: Dynamic N_TREES Schedule

backlog.spec: For the RandomForestRegressor, set max_features='sqrt' and min_samples_leaf=2. For the ExtraTreesRegressor, set max_features=0.5 and min_samples_leaf=1. This hybrid approach attempts to balance the inductive biases of both algorithms.
backlog.title: Balanced Random Forest approach

backlog.spec: Use the RDKit descriptors to calculate a 'complexity' score for each molecule (e.g., based on MolWt and number of heavy atoms) and use this score to weight the importance of the Morgan fingerprint bits (a form of feature-level weighting).
backlog.title: Descriptor-Based Weighting

incumbent.description: Average the predictions of a RandomForestRegressor and an ExtraTreesRegressor, both fit on the same Morgan+descriptor features and log1p target, to add ensemble diversity.

memo:
Incumbent: slot 17, RF+ExtraTrees average on Morgan 2048 + RDKit Properties descriptors, log1p target, max_features 'sqrt'. Loss 0.5146/0.5169 over 2 runs (baseline 0.6103; noise sd about 0.0070).

Helped: log1p target (-0.0369), 'sqrt' (-0.0237), Properties descriptors (-0.0182, replicated), RF+ET averaging (-0.0156, replicated).

Did not help: GBM swaps (LightGBM 0.5475 to 0.5683, CatBoost 0.5839 and 0.5966, XGBoost 0.5891 and 0.5972), a small LightGBM added to the ensemble (+0.0240), radius 3 (+0.0174), min_samples_leaf 5 (+0.0273), atom pairs (+0.0075), median blend (+0.0096), and top-100 feature selection (+0.0193). Target tweaks were within noise or worse.

Near misses, all within noise: radius-1 Morgan added (-0.0064), 10 top descriptors (-0.0056), 1000 trees (-0.0026), MACCS (-0.0023), weighted blend (-0.0007).

Next: combine the near misses (radius-1 bits, MACCS, 1000 trees) in one run and replicate it. Also try separate max_features for RF and ET. Skip more target transforms, GBMs and leaf-shrinking.
